content: 1. Indacaterol, when inhaled, and mefloquine both have the potential to prolong the QTc interval. This increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 3. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Mefloquine increases the levels of isradipine by decreasing its metabolism. This raises the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases the peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect is not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 7. Ivacaftor increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-glycoprotein, significantly increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 9. Mefloquine increases the levels of labetalol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is advised when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 12. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 13. Lidocaine increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Mefloquine increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 15. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Mefloquine decreases the levels of lumefantrine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Mefloquine decreases bile production; Coartem (lumefantrine) should be taken with food. 17. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor mavorixafor if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors, and reduce the mavorixafor dose if needed. 18. Mefloquine increases the levels of metoprolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Co-administration of mild CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam may cause higher systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 21. Mifepristone and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be used if available. 22. Mitotane decreases the levels of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 23. Mefloquine increases the levels of nadolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Mefloquine increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 26. Mefloquine increases the levels of nebivolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 28. Mefloquine increases the levels of nicardipine by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Mefloquine increases the levels of nifedipine by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Mefloquine increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. 31. Mefloquine increases the levels of nisoldipine by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Mefloquine and inhaled olodaterol both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 33. Osilodrostat and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 34. Osimertinib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes is recommended for patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 35. Ozanimod and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 36. Mefloquine and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Mefloquine increases the levels of penbutolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Phenobarbital and mefloquine decrease the effects of each other by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 39. Mefloquine increases the levels of pindolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Ponatinib increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Primaquine and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 43. Mefloquine increases the levels of propranolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 44. Quetiapine and mefloquine increase each other's toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Post-marketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or drugs causing electrolyte imbalance or QT prolongation. 45. Quizartinib and mefloquine increase each other's effects via QTc interval prolongation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 46. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 47. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 48. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 49. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Mefloquine increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 51. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of mefloquine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with a drug with a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 52. Mefloquine increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Patients with renal impairment receiving rivaroxaban with drugs that are combined P-gp and weak or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may have significant increases in exposure compared to patients with normal renal function and no inhibitor use. These increases may elevate bleeding risk; use rivaroxaban in this situation only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. 53. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 54. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of mefloquine via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 55. Sertraline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 56. Sorafenib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 57. Mefloquine increases the levels of sotalol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 59. Sunitinib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 60. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Talazoparib is a P-gp substrate; co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. 61. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 62. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 63. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 64. Ticagrelor increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 65. Mefloquine increases the levels of timolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 66. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 67. Valbenazine and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 68. Mefloquine increases the levels of verapamil by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 69. Voclosporin and mefloquine increase each other's effects via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 70. Mefloquine increases the effects of warfarin by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 71. Zileuton increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 72. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 73. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 74. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of mefloquine via QTc interval prolongation. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 75. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of mefloquine via QTc interval prolongation. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 76. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 77. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 78. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 79. Mefloquine decreases the levels of ritonavir by an unknown mechanism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 80. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 81. Mefloquine increases the levels or effects of topical ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 82. Mefloquine decreases the levels of valproic acid by an unspecified interaction mechanism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 83. Mefloquine increases the levels of acebutolol by decreasing its metabolism, raising the risk of arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 84. Adagrasib and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsade de Pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is recommended. 85. Mefloquine increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Reduce the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 86. Albuterol and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 87. Alfuzosin and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 88. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of amantadine via QTc interval prolongation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Mefloquine may enhance the QTc-prolonging effect of high-risk QTc-prolonging agents. 89. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of amiodarone via QTc interval prolongation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 90. Amisulpride and mefloquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended.
